thread_title: S. 'Wilkerson's White Knight' N. Walton Co, FL
breadcrumb: S. 'Wilkerson's White Knight' N. Walton Co, FL

posts.body_html:
This S. x moorei is famous for being able to produce gigantic white pitchers with a reddish throat. Cedric did a great job growing this plant and photographing it to its fullest potential. Usually plants growing in the wild look more outstanding than what we have in cultivation, but with this plant, it's just the opposite.

A little history behind this plant as I understand it: the clone originated from Bud Wilkerson's property in Walton Co, FL ( and Brooks Garcia was the lucky man who originally obtained, named, and distributed the plant). As of 2015, it's incredibly rare and has fetched some enormous sums of money both here in the states and in Europe due to the extreme demand and low availability. It doesn't seem like a plant that readily produces a lot of divisions, but it's still hard to say.

It took me years to finally get a piece of this plant, but I finally received a small, happy piece last winter. During 2014, it grew a bit but didn't produce any pitchers worth photographing. Finally, spring of 2015, the clone finally pushed out something worth seeing!

These traps below aren't at their fullest potential yet....much like S. leucophylla, the prized flush of pitchers are produced in the fall. This is still a pretty small rhizome, so it may be another year or two before I have this plant at its fullest potential.

Photos taken 4/17/15

Traps are still too young to produce the typical red throat patch:



But you can see a little bit of red here and there:






This clone has a "fattie" profile (in plants, it's a good thing, haha!):



And Wilkerson's white knight amongst its buddies:

posts.body_html:
I have yet to grown this plant to it's fullest potential. To recap, Cedric from France has shown the world just how amazing it can get, wilkerson's white knight can produce gigantic traps. here's a link to a picture by Cedric: farm9.staticflickr.com/8458/7971582908_cb55efef15.jpg

Now in comparison, here's Mike Wang's pathetic attempt to emulate such results. Still have a long ways to go, but this clone is gaining momentum year after year so hopefully next year I'll get some monster traps. It's very slow to divide, I literally have been able to get three divisions total out of it so far. Hopefully more can be made in the future.

Photos taken 9/15/16 and a few days earlier:






Grainy photo of the traps a day after they opened. Leuco alba washington Co, AL photobomb:

Calen and I were lucky enough to visit Buddy Wilkerson's property last weekend and fortunately we found 'WWK' still alive and thriving out in the bog. I wasn't able to get a good pic of the clone due to being crippled by a chainsaw a few hours before. Here are the few terrible pics I took hobbling on one leg:


Here's me trying to pose with WWK. I couldn't kneel down due to my chainsaw mishap. Notice the1/2 Daisy Dukes courtesy of the chainsaw:

^^^pitcher placement was unintentional but funny

Given it's very mixed heritage, this highly desirable clone is pretty tough to breed with, but when you get the right combinations and grow out enough seedlings, this clone can produce some stunning offspring!

Anyways, here are some updated pics of the clone, taken mostly on 10/13/21:







Hard to tell from the photos, but these have a very distinctive yellowish tinge this year! That trait has shown up with a few of the WWK crosses I've made in the past:
